plain-text — A reply with no tool calls — the simplest possible turn.
single-tool — One tool call, then an answer derived from its result.
parallel-tools — Several tool calls in one assistant message — exercises contentIndex fan-out.
tool-loop — Two or more assistant messages in one turn — the case where contentIndex restarts and partIds must not collide.
tool-error — A failing tool call the agent has to recover from.
abort — A turn cancelled while it is running.
steering — A steering message injected into a running turn.
tool-edit — An `edit` call — the one tool whose result carries a diff and a patch.
tool-write — A `write` call — a whole new file rather than an edit to one.
tool-bash — A `bash` call — stdout, exit status, and pi's truncation metadata.
tool-ls — An `ls` call — a directory listing, which reports its own entry limit.
tool-grep — A `grep` call — match counts and line truncation live in its details.
tool-find — A `find` call — path globbing, with its own result limit.
compaction — A manual compaction — `buildContextEntries` starts from the newest one, so this is the boundary history rebuilding and turn paging are built around.
bash-long-output — A bash call whose output is large enough for pi to stream updates and report truncation.
